story: Votan was present at a great building constructed by order of his uncle, intended to reach up to heaven. When the building failed, every people was given its own language, and Votan was charged by God to divide the lands of a region called Anahuac among them. Votan belonged to a royal lineage and established a kingdom called "Snake House" on a river, which eventually extended across a wider region to the Pacific coast. He also led seven families from a distant place to this continent and assigned them lands. Some accounts say Votan defeated a people called the Quiname, built a great city, and established an empire that covered much land. Votan made four trips back to a distant homeland. He was also known as "Lord of the Horizontal Wooden Drum" and as a jaguar god of darkness, and his name was one of twenty day names in a local calendar. Descendants of Votan were said to live in a village, forming a family bearing his name. Ritual objects associated with Votan were kept in a sanctuary until they were removed and burned in a public square by a bishop.
